text: The Adventurers' Guild at Mereward keeps a hole in the ground and a tally of who comes back out of it. Things climb out of the Maw, and somebody must be sent in. You are issued one (1) torch, one (1) ten-foot pole and a numbered tag for the recovery of remains, and you take the first stair with everyone else who ever took it. Thirty floors down, past a goblin warren, a dead dwarf-hold, a drowned temple, a wyrm upon its hoard, a mad mage's halls and an office of the keeping, the Maw proves a prison dug from both ends, and the whole descent proves a fall.

text: The moor road north out of Mereward ends where no road should, in a bank of mist that has lain across it longer than the Guild has kept records of the moor. Walk into it and it closes behind you, and what lies beyond is a valley shut upon every side: a village that bars its shutters from the street, a wood drowned when the mill-race was cut, an orchard planted upon graves, a lake that keeps a wedding, and a crag with a kept house upon it. Its lord is Corvane, who buried his bride, his abbot and his whole household, and who has not lain down these three hundred years. Four things may be done in his hall, and he has thought about all four.
